newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Security Council set to adopt Mideast draft.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Security Council set to adopt Mideast draft.

text.p: Security Council members were set to adopt a resolution on Saturday on the Middle East crisis that refers to a controversial tunnel in the Old City of Jerusalem in its introduction, but not in the operative part of the text, a U.N. spokesman said.

The rest of the draft, which carries no condemnation of Israel, calls for immediate cessation and reversal of all acts which have resulted in the aggravation of the situation and have negative implications for the Middle East peace process.

It also calls for the safety and protection of Palestinian civilians to be assured, for the immediate resumption of negotiations on the peace process on its agreed basis, and the timely implementation of agreements already reached.

During a daylong debate on Friday, the council heard a succession of speakers who criticised Israel's new right-wing government over an archaeological tunnel in Jerusalem close to the al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine, and accused it of dragging its feet on the Middle East peace process.

The opening of a second tunnel entrance, intended as a window for tourists on 2,500 years of history along the Western, or Wailing Wall, Judaism's holiest shrine, sparked Palestinian protests and three days of violence in which more than 50 Palestinians and over a dozen Israelis were killed.
Council members, who had been negotiating on the draft individually for much of the day, later gathered for informal consultations with a view to a formal meeting to adopt the resolution.
Arab diplomats insisted on the tunnel's being mentioned in the resolution while the United States was opposed. As a compromise, it would be referred to in the preamble, the U.N. spokesman said.
